correctness.rationale: Testing arbitrary antiderivatives of functions of \(y\) and \(z\) gives the two conditional laws exactly. If \(\mathbb E[x^2]=0\), invariance forces \(x=z=0\) and bounded completeness of the remaining scalar equation yields the equilibrium \((0,\alpha/\kappa,0)\). For nontrivial measures, stationarity of \(x^2/2\) and \(z^2/2\) gives the weighted mean formula, while the conditional \(z\)-law gives \(D=\mathbb E[(x-\lambda z)^2]=X_2-\lambda^2\mathbb E[z^2]\). Upper equality forces \(x=\lambda z\), hence constant \(z,x\), and bounded completeness reduces the support to the known equilibrium set. The symbolic verifier reproduces the algebra.
